newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude prices rise in ACCESS after hours - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude prices rise in ACCESS after hours - Nov 26.

text.p: U.S. crude oil prices rose modestly in active ACCESS after-hours trade on Tuesday ahead of the long Thanksgiving Day holiday weekend, traders said.

NYMEX January crude traded at $23.75 a barrel, up 12 cents a barrel early in the after-hours session after posting a similar upward move in the day's floor session. Traders said 889 crude lots changed hands early in the session, including 445 lots on the front-month contract.
Crude prices were in a holding pattern on doubts over the timing of Iraq's oil-for-food deal and expectations OPEC ministers would rollover production limits, traders said.
Traders said some bullish sentiment could emerge in the market on Wednesday on the American Petroleum Institute's estimate of a 2.034 million barrel draw in crude stocks nationwide.
The NYMEX market will end trade for the week following Wednesday's floor session for the Thanksgiving Day holiday weekend, and ACCESS trade will resume on Sunday.

December heating oil was traded at 71.85 cents a gallon on 623 lots traded overall, including 242 lots in the front- month contract. December gasoline was traded 69.05 cents a gallon on 360 lots, including 191 in the front-month contract, traders said.
